name: sql_transpile_capability
title: SQL Transpilation Service
summary: A capability to transpile SQL code between different dialects (e.g., MySQL to BigQuery, Spark to Snowflake) using the sqlglot library.

tools.name: transpile_sql
tools.description: Transpile one or more SQL statements from a source dialect to a target dialect.

params.name: sql
params.description: The SQL code string to transpile.

params.name: read_dialect
params.description: The source dialect (e.g., 'mysql', 'spark', 'postgres'). If None, it attempts to parse as standard SQL.

params.name: write_dialect
params.description: The target dialect (e.g., 'bigquery', 'snowflake', 'duckdb'). If None, it will use the source dialect if identity is True.

params.name: identity
params.description: If True and write_dialect is not specified, the source dialect will be used as both read and write dialect.

params.name: error_level
params.description: The desired error level for the parser (e.g., 'error', 'warn', 'none').

returns.name: transpiled_statements
returns.description: A list of the transpiled SQL statements, one per statement in the input SQL string array/list of statements separated by semicolons or newlines in the original input string (if applicable). Each element is a string representing a single transformed SQL statement array of strings.

returns.name: success
returns.description: Whether the transpilation process completed successfully without errors (if applicable). Note: The library returns a list of strings, so success is inferred from the presence of statements in the list or the absence of errors during execution).

returns.name: display_summary
returns.description: A human-readable summary of the transpilation result (e.g., 'Transpiled 2 statements from mysql to bigquery').

tools.implementation_notes: Call `sqlglot.transpile(sql=sql, read=read_dialect, write=write_dialect, identity=identity, error_level=error_level)`. The result is a list of strings. The 'success' and 'display_summary' fields in the return object should be constructed by the agent or the tool wrapper based on the result list.

uncertainties: The exact list of supported dialects is not explicitly provided in the tool, but can be inferred from the library's Dialect.get_or_raise method. If an invalid dialect is provided, it will raise an error.
